name: The Tutors Network (editorial placeholder)
summary: Representative enrichment / tutoring category entry — compare subject specialists carefully; Singapore’s arms race is optional in year one.
body: Singapore’s tuition culture is intense. Start from your child’s actual gaps, not neighbour panic. Ask for trial lessons, curriculum alignment (IB vs IGCSE vs MOE), and clear cancellation terms. Arrival-year guidance on expat.sg: one social and one physical activity before stacking weekday enrichment. Method centres (e.g. Kumon) and private tutors both fail when commute time exceeds learning gains — trial the specific teacher near home, not the brand brochure. Mandarin for non-Mandarin homes: brief the tutor whether you need MOE-primary readiness, IS optional-language support, or interest-keeping only — and trial before prepaid packages. Product map (Berries-style centres vs online 1:1 vs home tutor vs school bilingual tracks) lives in the Mandarin enrichment guide. Families aiming for AEIS / S-AEIS should brief tutors on MOE preceding-level maths (and secondary English) method, not generic ‘exam tips’ — and keep an international-school hold until MOE placement lands. Goal-date every engagement; open-ended retainers often mask missing in-school supports rather than fixing them. Family ops note: interim tutoring during an LS waitlist needs a written end date and goal — dual-career households otherwise convert wait anxiety into an open-ended invoice.
whenToEngage: Child has a defined subject gap after settling
AEIS / S-AEIS needs MOE preceding-level method
Comparing private tutor vs method centre commute cost
Non-Mandarin home needs MOE vs IS vs interest brief
